{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Richard H. Schelp''' (April 21, 1936, [[Kansas City, Missouri]], United States – November 29, 2010, [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], [[Tennessee]], USA) was an American [[mathematician]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.memorialparkfuneralandcemetery.com/obituary/user/show/template?id=7654 | title=Richard Schelp: In Celebration of a life well lived | publisher=Memorial Park Funeral Home & Cemetery] | accessdate=September 27, 2011}}</ref><ref name="Faudree Schelp">{{cite journal | last=Faudree | first=Ralph J. | title=My Friend and Colleague, Richard Schelp | journal=Combinatorics, Probability and Computing | volume=21 | issue=1–2 | date=2012 | issn=0963-5483 | doi=10.1017/S0963548311000630 | pages=1–9}}</ref>

Schelp received his bachelor's degree in mathematics and [[physics]] from the [[University of Central Missouri]] and his master's degree and doctorate in mathematics from [[Kansas State University]]. The adviser from his thesis was [[Richard Joseph Greechie]].<ref name="Mathematics Genealogy Richard Schelp">{{cite web | title=Richard Schelp | website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=11245 | access-date=2023-12-25}}</ref>
He was an associate mathematician and missile scientist at [[Johns Hopkins University]] for five years. He then became an instructor of mathematics at [[Kansas State University]] for four years. Finally in 1970 he became a professor of mathematics in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Memphis]]. He retired in 2001.

Schelp, an [[Erdős number]] one mathematician, was the fourth most frequent scholarly collaborator with [[Paul Erdős]].<ref name="Erdös Number Project">{{cite web | title=The Erdös Number Project | website=sites.google.com | date=2022-01-04 | url=https://sites.google.com/oakland.edu/grossman/home/the-erdoes-number-project | access-date=2023-12-25}}</ref><ref name="DBLP">{{DBLP|name=Richard H. Schelp}}</ref> He also collaborated on research with another top ten most frequent Erdős collaborator, [[Ralph Faudree]], who was based at the University of Memphis as well.<ref name="Erdös Number Project"/><ref name="University of Memphis Ralph Faudree">{{cite web | title=Dr. Ralph Faudree | website=The University of Memphis | date=1939-08-23 | url=https://www.memphis.edu/msci/people/rfaudree.php | access-date=2023-12-25}}</ref>
